correctness.rationale: Exactly defined icosahedral truncation has 60 vertices/90 edges, 12 pentagonal and 20 hexagonal faces. Every graph-distance-two edge is homotopic to a length-two original path and all facial boundary cycles have explicit scale-two triangular fillings, so the Rips complex is simply connected. Complete exact simplex enumeration yields (60,270,340,120,12); verified 120 elementary collapses remove every simplex of dimension above two. Euler characteristic 22 and integral Hurewicz plus homological Whitehead imply the claimed wedge of 21 two-spheres. The supplied deterministic standard-library checker independently rebuilds and verifies all finite data and every free coface; no extrapolation from samples is used.

originality.rationale: The closest fully inspected Platonic-solid classification treats different graph vertex sets and explicitly lists Archimedean solids as a prospective extension. Adamaszek's graph-power homotopy-equivalence criteria fail at the 5-cycles and non-centered K5 cliques of the truncated icosahedron. The inspected all-graph hexagon-packing theorem requires girth >=6 and edge-disjoint hexagons, whereas the present graph has girth five and hexagons sharing edges. Searches of equivalent names and reported prior claims identified no equivalent truncated-icosahedron scale-two wedge result. The inability to rule out unindexed prior work is recorded.
residual_risks: Equivalent previously circulated calculations might not be indexed by the consulted searches.

value.rationale: This iconic Archimedean fullerene is the natural extension of the 2023 Platonic-solid Rips classification. Its pentagonal and hexagonal boundaries interact at radius two; the proof determines the complete integral homotopy type, not just homology ranks. The sphere multiplicity 21, simple connectivity, and explicit finite simplicial collapse supply a meaningful exact test case for graph-square Rips topology and are not merely a renamed textbook result or tiny numeric increment.
